methods.label: Identify the corner pyramid
methods.explanation:
The congruent outer prisms determine the cut positions exactly. Their right-triangular end faces are congruent, so the two bottom segments on a unit edge have equal lengths. Each segment is therefore \(\tfrac12\). The repeated cuts give the same half-edge division in the perpendicular direction.

[Figure 1](figures/2005_AMC_12A_Q17_question_fig1.svg)

Work with the right-hand drawing. Let \(T\) be the cube vertex directly above \(W\). Let \(M\) and \(N\) be the midpoints of the two bottom edges starting at \(W\), and let \(P\) be the center of the bottom face.

For each pair of cuts, \(W\) lies in an outer triangular prism. The desired piece is the intersection of these two prisms. On the bottom face, one prism occupies the half next to \(W\) in one direction, and the other occupies the half next to \(W\) in the perpendicular direction. Their overlap is exactly the square \(WMPN\), of side \(\tfrac12\).

Both sloping cut planes bounding this piece pass through \(T\). Together with the two cube faces through \(WT\), they join the four edges of \(WMPN\) to \(T\). Thus the piece is a pyramid with square base \(WMPN\) and apex \(T\). Its perpendicular height is the cube edge \(TW=1\), even though the apex lies above a corner of the base.

Using pyramid volume equal to one-third of base area times height,
\[
V=\frac13\left(\frac12\right)^2(1)
=\boxed{\frac1{12}}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{A}\).
